page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 72 vCPUs across 36 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and includes 24 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It also includes 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. No GPUs are present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c5d.18xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core score of 66669.07 and a Passmark CPU score of 49974.67. Memory read bandwidth is also strong, reaching 3706.44 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 209.03 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform strongly, with Redis achieving 61.64 million operations per second. However, text generation for large language models is a notable tradeoff, showing weak performance with 52.33 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 7.25 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5d.18xlarge offers high compute density and fast local NVMe storage, making it highly efficient for workloads that require high-frequency CPU processing paired with low-latency local disk access. The lack of a GPU and the lower RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core represent clear tradeoffs, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or deep learning training. This instance is best suited for compute-heavy workloads, high-performance web serving, batch processing, distributed analytics, and high-throughput database operations.
